rationale:
PINS the `exports` relationship type, which measured 0 edges on 400 production-path corpus files while `exports: ExportInfo[]` was being filled the whole time. Two rules, counted separately because they have different triggers.

(a) THE UNIT'S PUBLIC TOP-LEVEL SURFACE. Scala has no `export` keyword in Scala 2, so its export surface is a VISIBILITY rule: a top-level declaration is part of the unit's API unless it carries private/protected. That is the rule the Java oracle derives from JLS 7.6, for the same reason — a JVM-family language with no module manifest expresses its export surface with access modifiers. Verified against 443 distinct corpus keys at 100% recall and 100% precision (script/m60/scala-imports-exports-oracle.ts, 300 files).

(b) SCALA 3 RE-EXPORT CLAUSES. `export scala.util.Try`, `export a.b.{List, Map => M}` and `export a.b.*`. Measured 0 occurrences on the Scala 2.13 corpus — this corpus has no `export` clause — so the rule is proven here rather than on the corpus, and the three forms were each probed against the pinned grammar (zero ERROR nodes) before this fixture was written. `export a.b.*` publishes the PATH, not one edge per member: the member set is not written in this file, so edges per member would be fabrications.

THREE GAPS THIS FIXTURE PINS, each found by the oracle disagreeing with the analyzer:
  - a public top-level TYPE ALIAS (`type Id = String`) is part of the surface; handleTypeAlias had no export path.
  - a backticked name must reach the surface WITHOUT its quoting: `createSymbol` strips (M60 #924) and seven export pushes did not, so `implicit val \`strip margin\`` published `\`strip margin\`` — a spelling no reference can write. The target below is `strip margin`, and the forbid row pins the backticked spelling as absent.
  - a `private[pkg]` declaration is NOT part of the surface outside its package, and neither is a private one, a member of a class/trait/object/enum, or an enum case.

The companion `object Point` is deliberately absent from the exports below: a companion shares its class's name, the class is the importable unit, and the F3 export-uniqueness gate rejects the duplicate.
